text: Sepolia is Ethereum's current recommended testnet for application and contract testing. Testnet ETH has zero value — and that's exactly what makes testnets both useful and misleading.
A clean testnet deployment proves the mechanics work: the deploy script's constructor arguments and ordering, the bytecode fitting the size limit, basic integration with testnet infrastructure.
What it doesn't prove: no real economic incentive to attack it, no real liquidity depth, no real gas congestion, no MEV pressure. Testnets see none of the adversarial conditions real funds attract.
Treat a testnet deployment as proof the mechanics work, not proof the economics are safe. That distinction is why later lessons add a pre-launch checklist and phased rollouts with value caps.
Testnets prove the script and the bytecode work. Lesson 13 builds that deployment script for real, with Foundry and Hardhat's actual syntax.
